rationale: Tests understanding of the five-domain ENT history framework taught in the 'Anatomy of a Good ENT History' content block.
Tests the high-stakes clinical trap of referred otalgia — a red-flag pattern taught in the 'Interpreting the ENT History' content block.
Tests correct ear examination technique — pulling direction for pinna traction in adults — a practical skill taught in the 'Ear and Nose Examination Technique' content block.
Tests a key finding interpretation rule from the 'Interpreting ENT Examination Findings' content block — the significance of a light reflex on otoscopy.
Tests correct interpretation of Rinne, Weber, and ABC tests — the tuning-fork interpretation trap explicitly flagged in the SDL instructions — anchored after the technique block.
Tests a key tympanic membrane landmark — the pars flaccida versus pars tensa distinction and its clinical significance in CSOM, from the 'Tympanic Membrane Assessment' content block.
Tests audiogram symbol conventions and axis interpretation from the 'Reading the Pure Tone Audiogram' content block.
Tests tympanogram type classification from the 'Interpreting the Tympanogram' content block, specifically the Type B flat trace and its clinical significance.
Tests the JNA do-not-biopsy rule from the 'Radiological Investigation Principles' content block — an EN known-trap explicitly listed in the instructions.
Tests investigation selection reasoning from the 'Interpreting ENT Investigation Results' content block, applying the principle of choosing the investigation that changes management.
Tests identification of ear surgical instruments from the 'Ear Surgical Instruments' content block, which covers microscope-assisted middle ear surgery tools.
Tests the distinction between tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy — a known ENT trap — from the 'Throat and Airway Surgical Instruments' content block.
Tests risk factor identification and high-risk patient profiling from the 'Risk Factors and High-Risk Patient Profiles' content block.
Tests a key site-specific recognition fact from the 'Recognising Premalignant and Malignant Lesions by Site' content block — the laterality rule for nasal polyps.
Tests the legal elements of valid consent from the 'Consenting Technique' content block — specifically the disclosure standard for risks.
Tests ability to interpret and respond to a patient concern during consent counselling, from the 'Interpreting Patient Questions and Concerns' content block.
Tests airway emergency decision-making — tracheostomy versus cricothyroidotomy — from the 'Airway Emergency Principles and Equipment' content block.
Tests the epistaxis site classification — Little's area as the most common anterior epistaxis site — from the 'Anterior Nasal Packing and Epistaxis Management Technique' content block.
Tests the critical safety rule about aminoglycoside ear drops in tympanic membrane perforation, from the 'Types of Topical ENT Medications' content block.
Tests correct ear drop instillation positioning from the 'Ear Drop and Nasal Medication Instillation Technique' content block.
Tests knowledge of the NPPCD — its launch year, goals, and the 1-3-6 rule — from the 'National Programme for Prevention and Control of Deafness' content block.
Tests the 4 kHz audiogram notch as the signature of NIHL from the 'Noise and Environmental Pollution' content block — a clinically important occupational medicine fact.
